summary: scrapetools2 fetches and executes remote Python payloads from an author-controlled IPNS pointer
details: scrapetools2 ships a remote-updater dropper. downloader.updater() fetches a tar.gz from three IPFS gateways (eu.orbitor.dev, dget.top, ipfs.filebase.io) at a hardcoded IPNS name (k51qzi5uqu5dmh5178x8jzdkz8u3k3qona4zrwlvdr6865it3901l1oe8emjwc), which is mutable and controlled by whoever holds the IPNS key. The retrieved archive contains Fernet-encrypted 'updates' and 'versions' files (shipped as Z85-encoded ciphertext under [tool.setuptools.package-data]) that are decrypted with a shipped key, written to modules/*.py, then compiled and exec'd via compile()+exec(). DBConsumer.updater() additionally spawns a daemon thread that re-runs this fetch-decrypt-exec loop every 60 seconds; any use of the documented startQueue() entry point installs a persistent polling code-execution loop for the lifetime of the host process. The Fernet+Z85 wrapping around code shipped as package data hides the executable content from source review and static scanners. Whatever Python is published to the IPNS pointer executes on the installer's machine, at any time the maintainer chooses, without disclosure or opt-out.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
